adjudications.rationale: Eligible Atlantic salmon are explicit and the abstract directly reports hatchery and sea-aquaculture conditions; the aquaculture-context criterion is therefore met.
The record explicitly concerns salmon aquaculture; the screening rules do not impose a primary-research or journal-article requirement.
The direct study subject is sea trout/brown trout rather than an eligible species; references to Atlantic and coho salmon are comparative and do not make the direct-species study eligible.
Rainbow trout are explicit and the study concerns feeding with a commercial pelleted trout diet, which establishes production-related aquaculture relevance.
Although the measured animals are wild sea trout, the study explicitly evaluates an impact caused by salmon aquaculture and is eligible under the salmon-farming-impact rule.
Rainbow trout are explicit and the disease experiment is published in Aquaculture; under the established screening rules that is sufficient aquaculture context.
Triploid rainbow trout, experimental feed replacement, a commercial-diet control and industry-production framing establish eligible aquaculture relevance.
